content: The term Resolution can refer to the following: 1. Logic: Resolution in logic is a rule of inference utilized in automated theorem proving, which is a method for deriving conclusions from premises in a logical system. 2. Law: In the legal context, a resolution is a formal written motion that is adopted by a deliberative body, such as a legislative assembly or board. 3. Music: In music theory, resolution refers to a technique where a dissonant chord or note transitions to a consonant one, creating a sense of closure or rest. 4. Meter: In the context of poetic meter, resolution involves replacing one long syllable (longum) with two short syllables (brevia). 5. New Year's Resolution: This refers to personal goals or commitments individuals set for themselves at the beginning of a new year. 6. Aircraft Incident: Resolution was the name of a Douglas DC-6 aircraft (BCPA Flight 304) that tragically crashed near San Francisco in 1953. Optics and Electronics 7. Display Resolution: This describes the level of detail or clarity on a display device, such as a computer monitor or television screen. 8. Temporal Resolution: This refers to the sampling frequency of a digital audio device, which determines how accurately it can capture changes over time. 9. Image Resolution: This is the measure of detail present in an image, often defined by the number of pixels or dots per inch (DPI). 10. Optical Resolution: This is the ability of an optical system, such as a microscope or telescope, to distinguish, detect, or record fine details. 11. Angular Resolution: This describes the capacity of an optical or other sensor to discern small objects or details at a distance. 12. Sensor Resolution: This refers to the precision or detail that a sensor can capture in its measurements. 13. Spatial Resolution: This is the ground area covered by a single pixel in an image, often used in satellite imagery or remote sensing. Business 14. Corporate Resolution: A legal document that specifies which individuals are authorized to act on behalf of a corporation in various matters. 15. Resolution plc: A major UK-based manager of life insurance funds, which was part of the FTSE 100 index. 16. Resolution Copper: A copper mining project located in Arizona, United States. Geography 17. Resolution Island (Nunavut): An island located in the Arctic region of Canada. 18. Resolution Island (New Zealand): An island situated in New Zealand. Naval Vessels 19. HMS Resolution: The name of several ships in the British Royal Navy. 20. HMNZS Resolution (A-14): A surveillance ship operated by the Royal New Zealand Navy. 21. Resolution-class Submarine: A class of submarines used by the British Royal Navy. Mathematics 22. Injective Resolution: A mathematical concept involving a series of injective objects in homological algebra. 23. Resolution of Singularities: A process in algebraic geometry used to simplify singular points on algebraic varieties. 24. Resolution in Logic: A proof calculus used in propositional and first-order logic to derive conclusions. Literature 25. Resolution Island (Fictional): A fictional island that serves as the setting for the novel Brown on Resolution by C.S. Forester. Other Uses 26. Conflict Resolution: The process of resolving disputes or conflicts between parties through negotiation, mediation, or other methods.
